text.p: Guns boomed and schoolchildren sang patriotic songs as President Suharto led Indonesia's celebrations on Sunday on the 52nd anniversary of independence from centuries of Dutch colonial rule.

Troops guarded routes to the presidential palace where Suharto presided over an independence day ceremony attended by members of parliament, government ministers, foreign dignitaries and veteran freedom fighters.
Guns boomed in a ceremonial salute at 10 a.m. (0300 GMT) -- the time when Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno proclaimed independence on August 17, 1945, in Jakarta.

The formal transfer of power from the Dutch, who had ruled Indonesia for more than 350 years before three years of Japanese occupation during World War II, came only in 1949 after intermittent and sometimes heavy fighting between colonial troops and a ragtag band of guerrillas.

Senior high school students selected from the country's 27 provinces hoisted the country's red and white flags at the ceremony. Junior high school students sang patriotic songs and military units held a brief parade.
Suharto made no speech but waved to the audience when leaving after the one-hour ceremony.
Jakarta was mostly deserted because of the holiday, but people gathered at the Freedom Square near the palace. Red-and-white bunting and lights decorated sidewalks on main thoroughfares.

Some said celebrations were muted because of economic woes hanging over the country. The rupiah fell to a historic low against the dollar on Friday and the stock market index has plunged more than 100 points since the beginning of the month, closing at its lowest level in the year on Friday.

Suharto attempted to allay the fears pervading markets on Saturday, using his annual state-of-the-nation address to promise tight monetary and fiscal policies and calling for a cutback in foreign borrowings.
